overview.title: About
overview.p1: Open Stream Environment is a Material Design 3 overlay plus a drag-and-drop control panel for Twitch and OBS. The overlay is served locally and added to OBS as a Browser Source.
overview.p2: Components: the overlay itself (shown in OBS), this control panel, standalone scenes, a Web Remote for phones and tablets, and an Elgato Stream Deck plugin.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.s1: In OBS add a Browser Source and paste the overlay URL from the Editor toolbar.
quickstart.s2: In Settings → Twitch set at least your channel name (chat connects anonymously).
quickstart.s3: Optionally connect DonationAlerts, YouTube and OBS WebSocket in Settings.
quickstart.s4: Add and arrange widgets in the Editor — changes apply to the overlay live.

editor.title: Editor
editor.p1: Drag widgets from the left library onto the canvas, or click one to add it.
editor.p2: Select a widget to edit its properties on the right. Drag to move it, use the corner handle to resize.
editor.p3: The Layers panel controls z-order; the Grid toggle helps with alignment. Copy this URL into an OBS Browser Source:

presets.title: Layout presets
presets.p1: The Presets block in the toolbar under the canvas saves the current widget layout under a name for quick layout switching.
presets.p2: A preset also saves the active 2D/3D themes, so loading one brings back its 3D widgets automatically.
presets.p3: Save overwrites the selected preset or creates a new one from the entered name; Delete removes a preset. Presets live in local-db.json and don't touch other settings.

themes.title: Themes
themes.p1: In Settings → Appearance themes are split into 2D and 3D groups. 2D themes set the base overlay palette: Material You (Material 3, default), Orbital (a Star Citizen HUD) and Pixel Perfect (a pixel look inspired by ShestakUI).
themes.p2: 3D themes are enabled separately and add neon 3D widgets: Star Citizen (Grim HEX) and Nuclear (a cold-war CRT terminal). The 3D group has an Off option that hides the 3D widgets entirely.
themes.p3: An active 3D theme overrides the 2D theme: the overlay, scenes and Wheel switch to its HUD and the 3D widgets become visible. Choosing Off returns to the saved 2D theme.
themes.p4: Create custom theme opens the 2D theme editor (4 seed colors, panel shape and a font pair). Pixel Perfect snaps widget text to the pixel grid (12/16/24/32px).

scenes.title: Scenes
scenes.p1: Each scene is a separate OBS source that replaces the gameplay view entirely (not drawn on top of it).
scenes.p2: Available scenes: Start, BRB, Main, Just Chatting, End and Fortune Wheel.
scenes.p3: Just Chatting shows a large chat feed and alerts, leaving room for your webcam on the left.
scenes.p4: Copy each scene's URL into its own OBS Browser Source and switch scenes from the remote or Stream Deck.

twitch.title: Twitch
twitch.p1: Chat connects anonymously and only needs the channel name.
twitch.p2: For follow/sub/cheer alerts you need a Twitch application and authorization.
twitch.s2: Set the Redirect URI to the value shown in Settings → Twitch.
twitch.s3: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret.
twitch.s4: Press Connect Twitch and approve the authorization in the browser.

donationalerts.title: DonationAlerts
donationalerts.p1: Donations automatically increase the goal counter and trigger an alert.
donationalerts.s2: Set the Redirect URI to the value shown in Settings → DonationAlerts.
donationalerts.s3: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret, then press Connect DonationAlerts.

youtube.title: YouTube
youtube.p1: Live chat and live events (Super Chat, new members) via the YouTube Data API v3.
youtube.s1: Create an OAuth client in console.cloud.google.com.
youtube.s2: Enable the YouTube Data API v3 for the project.
youtube.s3: Set the Redirect URI shown in Settings → YouTube and paste the Client ID/Secret.
youtube.s4: Connect, then optionally set a Video ID as a fallback for live-chat lookup.

obs.title: OBS WebSocket
obs.p1: Requires OBS 28+ with the WebSocket server enabled (Tools → WebSocket Server Settings).
obs.p2: Scene mapping translates logical remote names into your actual OBS scene names.
obs.p3: You can also define custom RAW commands, camera angles (multicam) and camera filters, triggered by Twitch points or manually.
obs.p4: The Camera and Microphone fields set the sources for the webcam and microphone toggle buttons in the remote.

soundboard.title: Soundboard
soundboard.p1: Map a Twitch channel-points reward to a sound file and an image/GIF animation.
soundboard.p2: Adjust the volume and queue mode, then test each sound from the panel.

streamdeck.title: Stream Deck
streamdeck.p1: The Elgato plugin switches scenes: Start, BRB, Wheel, Talk and End.
streamdeck.p2: Set custom per-scene icons in Settings → Stream Deck.

remote.title: Web Remote
remote.p1: Open from a phone or tablet on the same Wi-Fi network using the address shown in the header.
remote.p2: From the remote you can switch scenes, control the wheel and death counter, send test alerts, run OBS commands, change the theme, switch cameras and trigger effects.
remote.p3: The Wheel tab holds the wheel settings (command, participants, list position, volume, speed) and the participant list: add and remove viewers right from the remote.
remote.p4: Next to the webcam there is a microphone mute button — set the audio input name in Settings → OBS.

terminal.title: Terminal and commands
terminal.p1: The Terminal button in the header opens the built-in console: it shows server and integration logs in real time.
terminal.p2: Type commands in the input (e.g. scene brb, death +1, wheel spin, sim sub user, theme pixel, status). Type help for the full list.
terminal.p3: Tab autocompletes commands and arguments (scenes, sounds, cameras, filters). The search field in the terminal header filters logs by text, and logs <level> filters by level.

wheel.title: Fortune Wheel
wheel.p1: Viewers join by typing the entry command in Twitch chat.
wheel.p2: Elimination mode removes one participant per spin until the final winner.
wheel.p3: The Wheel button in the header opens the wheel settings panel, with a participants panel (search and clear) next to it.
wheel.p4: Use Generate wheel and Spin the wheel, plus the music volume and spin speed settings.
wheel.p5: In the Web Remote, the Wheel tab mirrors these settings and lets you manage participants from your phone.

debug.title: Debug
debug.p1: The Debug button in the header opens a panel with test buttons: alerts (follow, sub, gift, cheer, donation) and a test chat.
debug.p2: Integration debug logs (such as heartbeat events) are shown below. Use Clear to remove accumulated logs.

settings.title: Application settings
settings.p1: Port changes the local server port and requires an app restart.
settings.p2: Appearance manages overlay themes; Export/Import saves the full config.json together with media files (it contains secrets — don't share it).
settings.p3: Language switches the whole interface between English and Russian.

data.title: Data and backups
data.p1: Exporting settings saves the full config.json plus all files from the media folder (sounds, images, GIFs) in a single file.
data.p2: On import, media files are automatically restored into the media folder.
data.p3: The media cleanup command in the terminal removes unused media files. Window sizes and positions are remembered, and server logs are written to the logs folder.
